historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: organic revenue growth (FY2026 guide 3.5-4.5% organic, ~2pp price) plus mix; the equity CAGR is not usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5y 20.0%, 3y 29.8%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (5y 8.4%). Allegion's book equity was near zero/negative after the 2013 spin and has been depressed by buybacks, so its growth rate is a base-effect artefact. Revenue CAGRs include ~3pp/yr of acquired revenue (Stanley Access Technologies FY2022, ELATEC FY2025) and a COVID-depressed FY2020 base; EPS CAGR benefits from buybacks and margin recovery.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR series uses FCF less SBC (equity-award tax proxy only available for FY2025). The SBC-adjusted 3y and 5y FCF CAGRs track reported FCF closely (SBC is <1% of revenue and stable), so SBC is not funding a growing share of reported growth. The 3y FCF CAGR (20.9%) is flattered by a weak FY2022 base (inventory build, $923m Stanley Access acquisition year).

scenario_narratives.base: Allegion compounds as a specification-locked incumbent. FY2026 delivers the raised guide (7.5-8.5% reported, 3.5-4.5% organic) with H2 margin expansion as the May price increases catch up with tariffs. From FY2027 revenue grows 4-5% organically -- low-single-digit volume from US institutional/non-residential construction and aftermarket replacement, ~2% price, and electronics mix -- decelerating to 3% by year 10. The adjusted EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) edges from 25.1% to 26.5% as electronics/access control grows faster than mechanical and International's ERP and restructuring issues ($10m savings) wash out. Capex stays ~2.4% of sales; growth consumes ~12c of working capital per incremental dollar of revenue. Terminal at 2.5% growth, capped at 16x FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The spec pipeline management calls the strongest in the CEO's tenure converts into 6-7% organic growth for three years: data centres grow from ~5% of non-residential revenue, institutional (education, healthcare, government) spending holds, and ELATEC's brand-agnostic readers pull electronic lock and credential attach rates up. Europe recovers to flat-to-positive organic growth. Mix and pricing power in a top-five oligopoly lift the adjusted EBITDA margin to 28% by year 8. Terminal growth 3%, exit capped at 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The US non-residential construction cycle turns under higher-for-longer rates: FY2026 finishes below the guide as the pre-buy ahead of the May price increase unwinds (the Q3 air pocket management itself flagged), and FY2027 revenue falls 3% with negative operating leverage taking the margin to 23.5%. Germany/Europe stays in decline, International integration of the six-plus bolt-ons disappoints, and recovery is slow -- growth never exceeds 3% and the margin settles at 24.5%, below today's. Debt-funded M&A leaves less room to buy back through the trough. Terminal growth 2%, exit capped at 13x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Allegion is a mature, specification-driven security-hardware franchise with a large replacement installed base, valued on unlevered owner FCF (SBC expensed, share count flat) with a component-built margin and a moderate-cycle scenario spread. The value question is not survival but how much organic growth and margin expansion the price already assumes; the 16x base terminal cap keeps a long-duration, terminal-heavy valuation from depending on perpetuity maths.
key_risks_to_valuation: US non-residential construction downturn (majority of revenue) -- the bear path's -3% FY2027
Pre-buy ahead of the May 2026 price increase masking a Q3/Q4 2026 organic air pocket
European/German organic decline and lower International margins persisting
Integration risk across six-plus 2025-26 acquisitions; future M&A spend is not modelled
Terminal value is ~57% of base enterprise value (50-61% across scenarios); implied exit 13-18x FCF sits below the ~20x EV/unlevered-FCF the market pays today, so no multiple expansion is assumed
Pillar Two / Irish domicile: cash tax rate could rise above the modelled 18.5%

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 125.00-183.11
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001579241): FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q; ALLE_Metrics.csv for history
data_sources.qualitative: ALLE_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): Q2 2026 results and raised FY2026 guidance of 2026-07-23

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted point-in-time: 85.06m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover/balance sheet) + 0.3m incremental share-based dilutive securities (Q2 2026 diluted EPS reconciliation) = 85.4m. Q2 2026 weighted diluted count was 86.0m; the point-in-time figure is lower because $160.6m was repurchased in H1 2026. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $29.8m, plus $8.1m 'other financing activities' outflow (XBRL ProceedsFromPaymentsForOtherFinancingActivities) used as a conservative proxy for net-share-settlement tax withholding net of option-exercise proceeds; Allegion publishes no combined figure.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted in USD. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.2%. Debt ~$2.0bn of senior notes at ~5% pre-tax (~4.1% after tax) against ~$13bn market cap (~13% debt weight) -> WACC ~8.5%. One WACC for all scenarios: construction-cycle risk is charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Allegion reports under US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease expense ($69.1m FY2025) is already inside operating income and hence inside EBITDA; there are no finance leases of note. Operating lease liabilities ($191.2m at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (US operating company, moderately cyclical security-hardware industrial; SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations; adaptations applied: leases (B), risk charged once, USD WACC). Fresh build, no prior DCF. FY0 = FY2025: revenue $4,067.3m, OCF $783.8m, capex $98.1m (XBRL PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets; the CSV's FY2025 CapEx cell is blank because the tag changed from PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment) -> reported FCF $685.7m; owner FCF = 685.7 - 37.9 - 0 = $647.8m (15.9% of revenue). Interest income ($12.0m FY2025) is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt ($1.71bn), so there is no net-cash pile to double count. Owner FCF is a levered, post-interest figure (~$98m cash interest); the engine projects unlevered flows and deducts net debt once, so the FY2026 unlevered margin (~17.5%) sits above the FY2025 levered owner margin by roughly the after-tax interest bill -- that is consistent, not a carried one-off. FY0 adj. EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) = (GAAP EBITDA 989.2 + SBC 29.8)/4067.3 = 25.05%; restructuring and acquisition costs are left inside (they recur with the bolt-on programme). Growth in FY2026 includes acquired revenue (ELATEC, Next Door, Trimco, Nova, DCI) whose purchase price is already in the 2026-06-30 net debt; from FY2027 the paths are organic-plus-price only, so no future M&A spend is charged and none of its revenue is credited. Net debt: total debt $2,031.3m (senior notes + current portion, 2026-06-30 10-Q) less cash and restricted cash $320.6m (2026-06-30). Buybacks: $80m FY2025, $160.6m H1 2026 -- a genuine repurchaser, so the flat share count is being funded.
inputs.cash_tax_basis: FY2025 cash taxes paid $121.2m on pre-tax income ~$768m (15.8%); unlevered (adding back the interest shield) ~16-17% of EBIT. Irish-domiciled group with Pillar Two 15% minimum tax; H1 2026 book ETR 19.2%. Path ramps 17% -> 18.5%.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the midpoint of the raised 7.5-8.5% reported-growth guide (acquisitions + price). Thereafter mid-single-digit organic growth: Americas non-residential spec pipeline and data centres offset a soft Europe; electronics mix and pricing add ~150bp of margin over a decade.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): revenue is tied to a construction cycle management has flagged a near-term air pocket in, and leverage rose with the 2025-26 bolt-ons -- but there is no solvency or refinancing risk (next material maturity 2027-28, ~2x net debt/EBITDA). Base 50%: the raised FY2026 guide and spec pipeline support mid-single-digit organic growth. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs sustained above-trend organic growth AND a European recovery AND 250bp of margin expansion -- several independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
